correctness.rationale: The fiber-privacy lemma is valid: a proper repeated fiber in one coordinate forces each member to use symbols globally unique in the other two coordinates, otherwise a descendant has an outside codeword tied with or closer than a parent. Consequently repeated-fiber memberships are disjoint across coordinates. Counting used symbols gives \(R_i-G_i\ge n-q\), and for \(n>q\), \(G_i\ge1\), whence \(3(n-q)\le n-3\). The diagonal and three-group constructions meet the resulting bound. An independent direct descendant check verified the constructions for \(2\le q\le18\); this finite check is supplementary to the symbolic proof.
